The main failure symptom is that the PosixParser, when parsing with stopAtNonOption=true, ignores unrecognized tokens that start with a dash '-'. The test case tries parsing arguments ["-z", "-a", "-btoast"] with stopAtNonOption=true and expects that option "-a" is not set because the unknown option "-z" should cause the parser to stop parsing options.

The current bug report summarizes this: "PosixParser doesn't handle properly unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when stopAtNonOption is enabled, the token is simply ignored." It gives an example with a known option "a" and an unknown option "-z" that is ignored rather than stopping the options parsing.

The recent similar bug reports also point out issues with PosixParser's stopping behavior when encountering "--" or when bursting tokens with non-option characters, confirming that the parser's logic around stopping at non-options and token parsing is problematic.

The key method involved should be PosixParser.parse(Options, String[], boolean) which takes the options, command line arguments, and stopAtNonOption flag. However, attempts to retrieve the exact code snippet for this method encountered multiple matches and ambiguity among available parse methods in Parser and CommandLineParser interfaces.

Next, I will explore PosixParser class methods related to option parsing or token handling that might be involved in this malfunction, to understand how the parser handles unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when stopAtNonOption=true.

I will first check the class PosixParser to find parse methods in particular.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
